title: Installing Python

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
Installing Python from the official distribution and checking its version ensures the interpreter and pip belong to the intended setup.
CORE EXPLANATION

Install Python with the official installer for your operating system from python.org. Windows provides the Python Launcher; macOS and Linux may use a versioned Python 3 command. Reopen the terminal and verify the version after installation.

spans.code: Version strings vary by installed Python and pip.

spans.text:
Terminal commands
`python --version` — Prints the active Python interpreter's version; your platform may use `python3` or `py` instead.
`python -m pip --version` — Shows pip attached to that interpreter; `python -m pip` makes the selected Python explicit.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: If several Python versions are installed, verify which interpreter a project actually uses.

spans.title: Important detail
spans.text: The executable may be named python3 or py, depending on the platform.

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: Do not remove the operating system's Python or install packages globally without a reason.
COMMON MISTAKES
Keep the interpreter, pip, and project packages in the same virtual environment.
